name: Audi Sport quattro S1 E2
hook: Audi tried an experimental twin-clutch gearbox in it in 1985, an ancestor of the paddle-shift boxes every fast car uses now.
story: October 1985, Sanremo. Audi's Group B project is running out of road. The five-cylinder quattro proved that four-wheel drive wins rallies, but the little mid-engined Peugeots and Lancias now out-handle it everywhere. So Audi cuts the wheelbase, hangs enormous wings off both ends, and moves the radiator behind the driver to drag weight rearward. That car is the S1 E2. Walter Röhrl and Christian Geistdörfer take it onto Italian asphalt and simply leave. They beat the newly crowned world champion, Timo Salonen, by more than six minutes. It is the only world championship rally an E2 ever wins. Seven months later a fatal crash in Corsica ends the class: the governing body outlaws Group B from the following season, and Audi walks away from rallying. The E2 does not retire quietly. In 1987 Röhrl drags one up Pikes Peak, then a gravel road with 156 bends, in 10 minutes 47.85 seconds. Outright win. Last word.
description: The Sport quattro S1 E2 was Audi's final Group B rally car, developed by Audi Sport during 1985. A shortened, Kevlar-bodied quattro shell carries a 2,110 cc turbocharged five-cylinder with an officially quoted 473 horsepower, driving all four wheels through a Torsen centre differential. The radiators sit at the back for balance, behind the driver. Roughly twenty works cars were built. It is the loudest, most winged expression of the era that made all-wheel drive normal.

stats.label: Drivetrain
stats.value: Permanent four-wheel drive, Torsen centre diff
